note: The shape of this application, declared by the application itself, so an assessment tool can draw where its findings actually sit instead of guessing from URLs or showing a stock diagram. Companion to checks.json (what may be tested) and findings.json (what can be fixed). This service is one small Express deployable: the modules below are parts of that one process, not separate services, and the map says so. Keep this honest — a component here must correspond to real code in src/, and its routes to routes that exist.

components.name: Browser
components.detail: Anyone who can reach the service. There is no front-end build; the root route serves one page of HTML.

components.name: Public site
components.detail: The landing page and the service's own health and version endpoints. Unauthenticated by design.

components.name: Session login
components.detail: Signs a user in as one of the seeded tenants and sets the session cookie everything else reads.

components.name: Invoices API
components.detail: Lists the caller's invoices and returns one by id. The per-record ownership check is the seeded flaw.

components.name: Debug configuration
components.detail: Unauthenticated endpoint that lists every account and its latest invoice id. It is what turns an unguessable id into a guessable one, so it is the chain enabler for the invoice flaw.

components.name: In-memory data
components.detail: Two invented tenants and four invoices held in process memory (src/data.js). No database, no real data, nothing persisted.
